body:
"2026 is the new 2016" is a social media trend in which people post photos and videos in the style of 2016: grainy phone pictures, heavy filters, dog-ear Snapchat effects and flower crowns. It began on New Year's Eve 2025 and spread quickly through January 2026.

How it started

Reports trace the trend to a TikTok montage of 2016 moments posted by the user @taybrafang on New Year's Eve 2025. The #2016 hashtag grew to more than 2.3 million posts on TikTok, and celebrities including Charlie Puth, Selena Gomez, John Legend and Reese Witherspoon joined in, according to press coverage.

What people post

  • Throwback photos from 2016, often with the VSCO-era look.
  • Recreations of the period's makeup and fashion: bold brows, statement outfits and heavy editing.
  • Playlists and audio from that year.

Why it caught on

Writers at Forbes and elsewhere link it to fatigue with AI-generated content and heavily curated feeds. The trend grew out of an ironic joke among younger users about the "Great Meme Reset", the wish to return to an internet before AI-generated content filled it, and it turned into a sincere nostalgia.

What it tells us

Nostalgia cycles are not new, but a ten-year gap is short. Part of the appeal is that 2016 feels both recent and obviously dated, and the photos from that year look like they came from a more casual web.
